title: Word order with eikö with singular owners
summary: Build singular-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.
prerequisiteSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
objectives: Build singular-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Build singular-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.
Put minulla, sinulla, and hänellä immediately after eikö. Keep ole separate, after the owner, then finish with the complete partitive noun.
keyPoints: Build singular-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.

steps: Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put minulla next. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive autoa (“a car”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put sinulla next. sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive palloa (“a ball”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put hänellä next. hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive kynää (“a pen”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put minulla next. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive peliä (“a game”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.

Do not lose ole or the noun ending while arranging the question.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
kynä + -ä = kynää. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.
